MOTOR ACCIDENTS CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, MAVELIKARA APPELLANT/PETITIONER:
 KRISHNANKUTTY, VARIKKOLIL PADEETTATHIL VEEDU, EREZHA  SOUTH, CHETTIKULANGARA P.O,
BY ADVS.
SRI.GEORGE VARGHESE(PERUMPALLIKUTTIYIL)
SRI.P.J.JOE PAUL RESPONDENTS/RESPONDENTS:

1 THULASEEDHARAN  PARAVILA PUTHEN VEEDU, NEDUVATHOOR,
 KOTTARAKKARA, KOLLAM- 691 506.
 2 THE MANAGING DIRECTOR  KSRTC, THIRUVANANTHAPURAM - 695 001.
 BY ADV  SRI. ALEX ANTONY SEBASTIAN P.A.
 THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 11.12.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 M.A.C.A No.666 of 2018  2  2024:KER:93961  JUDGMENT Dated this the 11th day of December, 2024
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.)No. 235/2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mavelikara is the appellant herein.

The respondents in the O.P.
are the respondents.

The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
Krishnankutty vs Thulaseedharan on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135344520/
1 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained on account of the accident that occurred on 21.06.2007.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. According to the petitioner, on 21.06.2007 at about 4 p.m., while he was pedalling his bicycle from Thattarambalam to Kayamkulam public road, a KSRTC bus bearing reg.No. KL-15-5758 driven by the 1st respondent dashed against his bicycle and hit him down.
As a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
The 1st respondent is the driver, and the 2nd respondent is the employer of the 1st respondent.
According to him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs. 1,80,000/-.
3. The 2nd respondent filed a written statement disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further 2024:KER:93961 contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
4. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A11.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.78,726/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
8. Heard Sri. P.J. Joe Paul, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri. Alex Antony Sebastian, learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent.
9. The Point: In this case, the accident is admitted.
Though in the written statement the 2nd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.
The petitioner has produced Ext.A5, copy of the charge sheet involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending 2024:KER:93961 vehicle, in respect to the above accident.
In the light of the above charge sheet, negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.
Therefore, the 2nd respondent, being the employer of the 1st respondent is liable to pay the compensation, which is liable to be awarded in this case.
10. The petitioner was aged 53 years on the date of the accident, on 21.06.2007.
According to the petitioner, he was a Coolie, earning Rs.4,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed his income only at Rs.3,000/-.

Since he could not prove the income claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Krishnankutty vs Thulaseedharan on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135344520/
2

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Krishnankutty vs Thulaseedharan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], his notional income is fixed at Rs.6,000/-.

entities.text: Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.12,000/-, which, according to the petitioner is on the lesser side.
Considering the fact that the petitioner was hospitalised as inpatient for 18 days and he had to take rest for about six months, the compensation awarded for loss of earning is on the lesser side.
Since the notional income is now fixed at Rs.6000/-, compensation towards loss of earning is enhanced to Rs.36,000/- (6000 x 6).
12. The petitioner produced Ext.A10 - disability certificate issued by the medical board, showing that he has a permanent disability of 15%.
The tribunal reduced the same to 8% without assigning any reasons.
Therefore, he prayed for taking the disability as 15%.

As per Ext.A6 wound certificate, the petitioner sustained lacerated wound 7 x 0.5 cm bone deep on the front of scalp with swelling of surrounding area extending to the forehead, abrasion bridge of nose and superficial laceration upper and lower legs.
As per Ext.A7 discharge card issued from the Medical College Hospital, Kottayam, he sustained fracture shaft of radius left and fracture arch of atlas.

As per Ext.A10 disability certificate issued by PW1, the Assistant Professor of Orthopaedics, Government Medical College Hospital, Alappuzha,
recorded the injury sustained by the petitioner are, (i)there is 400 limitation of dorsiflexion, 300 limitation of polar flexion, 100 limitation of pronation and supination of left forearms due to post traumatic stiffness of wrist and left forearm.
(ii). Grip and grasp strength of left hand is weak.

(iii).
Movement of cervical spine limited terminally due to cervical spondylosis which is a post traumatic sequelae.
13. It was on the basis of the above findings, a competent Doctor who examined him, has certified with a reasons that permanent disability suffered by him is 15%.
However, the tribunal, without assigning any valid reasons, arrived at a conclusion that the petitioner has only 8% permanent disability.
If the Tribunal finds that that the disability certificate is not 2024:KER:93961 acceptable

,
it could have referred the petitioner to a Medical Board.
Therefore, considering the fact that that the petitioner is a coolie, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve Ext.A10 disability certificate.
Accordingly, his disability is fixed at 15%.

Since, on the date of accident, he was aged 53 years, 10 %
of his income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 11, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.1,30,680/-.
14.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioner, is on the lower side.
The petitioner was treated as an inpatient for 18 days.
Because of the injuries sustained by him, he had to take rest for a considerable period.
In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lesser side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.

15. Towards the head compensation for loss of amenities, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/-,
which according to the learned counsel for the petitioner, is on the lower side.

The petitioner was Krishnankutty vs Thulaseedharan on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135344520/
3 treated as an inpatient for 18 days.

entities.text: Krishnankutty vs Thulaseedharan on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Because of the injuries sustained by him, he had to take rest for a 2024:KER:93961 considerable period.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards loss of amenities is on the lesser side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
16.
Towards transportation expenses, the Tribunal has only awarded an amount of Rs.500/-.
From the evidence it appears that after the incident, the petitioner had to go at first to Kottayam Medical College and thereafter to ESIC Model Hospital, Kollam.

Therefore, Rs.500/- awarded towards transportation is on the lesser side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.3000/-.
17.
Towards extra nourishment, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.500/-, which, according to the petitioner is also on the lesser side.

Considering the fact that the petitioner was hospitalised as inpatient for 18 days and he had to take rest for a considerable period, the compensation awarded for extra nourishment is on the lesser side, and hence it is enhanced to Rs.7,000/-.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.2,55,726/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

Table 1  Sl. Head of claim Amount awarded by The amount given   No. the Tribunal(Rs) appeal (Rs.)
 1 Loss of earnings 12000 36000  2 Loss of earnings (partial) - -
 3 Transportation 500 3000  4
Extra nourishment 500 7000

6 Damage to bicycle --- ---  7 Medical expenses & bystanders 5346 5346  expenses  3200 3200  8 Pain and sufferings 20000 50000  9 Compensation for permanent 31680 130680  disability & loss for earning power  10 Compensation for loss of amenities 5000 20000  in life
Total 78,726

Amount enhanced Rs.1,77,000/-
20.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 2 nd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.2,55,726/- (Rupees Two lakh Fifty five thousand seven hundred and twenty six Krishnankutty vs Thulaseedharan on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135344520/
4 Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
21. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, 2024:KER:93961 without delay, as per rules.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE S.M.K.
